title: The Deacon Is Dead
description: THE VELVET HEARSE, "The Deacon Is Dead" (an imaginary 1972 single): the band plays the funeral home the night before the bass player's funeral, because their instruments are locked in the hearse with him. Coffin, urn, a hearse spring, a likembe tuned to seven equal steps, a friction drum, beads, coins, a brake drum and a door. No bass, no voice, no reed.

sections.development: the door creaks; three knocks on the lid; coins; the likembe picks up
the likembe alone, then the three knocks
the hook: urn, coffin and spring split the bass line; every second bar drops out for the knocks; friction drum and brake drum join
drums alone: urn, beads, coins, rim, scrape, the knocks
the floor: the friction drum talks and laughs over likembe, spring and urn
half time, one step of seven higher every bar, home an octave up
two stabs, silence, three knocks from inside the coffin, the door
the hook hot; every knock bar ends with a knock from inside
the last hit, the spring as a laser, the coins spill, one knock from inside, the door
